transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-09-22
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Riley O'Connor (Redwood); Liam Chen (Redwood Ops); Sana Kapoor (NovaPay Head of ML); Tom Reynolds (NovaPay Platform Eng); Aisha Mbaye (NovaPay CTO); Ethan Li (NovaPay SRE); Priya Desai (NovaPay Product)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync — throughput optimization. Discussed recent benchmark results, batching/config changes, observed p99 latencies under load, and next steps to run a longer continuous test.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we have 45 minutes, we'll run through the recent test runs Diego did, then talk configs and next steps. Sana and team, anything to add up front?
[00:10] Sana: no, thanks Maya. we mainly want to understand headroom for our peak, and whether dedicated is required or hosted will do, also curious about cost delta if we push concurrency.
[00:18] Diego: cool. quick recap — last week we ran three 1-hour runs: baseline (batching off), continuous batching at 20ms window, and continuous batching at 50ms window. we targeted concurrency 32 for the first set.
[00:28] Tom: just to clarify, when you say concurrency 32, that's per model shard or total?
[00:33] Diego: good question — that's per shard for the current ded-setup; in hosted it maps to N worker processes. there was some confusion in the doc where it said per-node, I'll update that column.
[00:41] [00:41] Riley: note, the benchmark sheet has a mis-typed column header — "concurrency_per_node" should be "concurrency_per_shard" — small transcription error.
[00:48] Maya: Diego, can you give the headline numbers?
[00:50] Diego: yep. baseline: p50=210ms, p90=820ms, p99=1.7s at 20 QPS sustained; batching 20ms window: p50=190ms, p90=560ms, p99=1.0s; batching 50ms: p50=210ms, p90=600ms, p99=1.2s but throughput went up ~1.8x. cost per token dropped ~28% on estimated infra.
[01:10] Ethan: those p99s still look high for our SLOs, we need p99 < 800ms during peak at 100 QPS.
[01:16] Diego: understood — two levers we discussed: increase target concurrency (from 32 to 64), and change the queuing/backpressure policy to prioritize low-latency requests and cap queue depth. also enable prefix KV cache for repeated user prompts.
[01:29] Aisha: If we increase concurrency, do we risk worse tail because of scheduling?
[01:33] Liam: there's a tradeoff — higher concurrency allows better GPU occupancy due to batching, but at extreme concurrency you can hit CPU scheduling and queue spike; that's why we tune the batching window and have a cap.
[01:44] [01:44] Tom: is there a recommended concurrency per GPU spec? we're on A100-sim nodes in staging currently.
[01:49] Diego: for A100 80GB, for this model family we saw sweet spot around 48-64 concurrency per shard for throughput. below 32 you lose TBW efficiency, above 80 you see increased p99.
[01:58] Sana: what's the impact on cost? Maya you mentioned 28% reduction at 50ms batching?
[02:03] Maya: yes, roughly 25-30% depending on token mix and cache hit rate. We can run the full calc once Diego updates the per-run token counts in the sheet.
[02:12] [02:12] Diego: another observation: our continuous batching implementation had a small bug where the kv cache wasn't being keyed by user id for replay tests; that lowered effective cache hit during the replay. fixed now for staging run.
[02:22] Priya: what about queueing/backpressure — can Redwood drop or reroute low-priority requests when the queue gets deep?
[02:27] Diego: yes — we have routing and priority levels. options: shed lower-priority, reroute to a cheaper quantized model variant, or return a fast fallback response. we demoed rerouting in the tech deep-dive last month.
[02:36] [02:36] Sana: we can't shed any requests during checkout flows — but for background artifact processing it's ok. we'll need per-route policies.
[02:41] Diego: per-route is supported — you can set priority levels by endpoint or by API key.
[02:46] Maya: let's align on the test plan — Diego to push new config (concurrency 64, batching 20ms + 50ms variants, queue cap 200ms latency-based), run a 12-hour continuous load that mirrors production hourly bursts, and then share the result sheet.
[02:58] Tom: are you able to replay sticky user sessions? we need to ensure per-user KV cache behavior is realistic.
[03:04] Diego: yes, Tom — but we need you to provide sticky user key mapping in the trace CSV. Sana can we get that?
[03:09] Sana: yes, I'll export a sample trace with user keys and p95/p99 windows; should have that by tomorrow.
[03:14] [03:14] Riley: small note — the staging cluster is slightly smaller than your expected prod capacity. results will show headroom, but we'll add a projected prod run in the sheet that scales up capacity linearly.
[03:22] Aisha: regarding private deployment — if hosted can't meet p99, will dedicated NovaPay-only pool be better?
[03:27] Diego: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and isolates noisy neighbors, which helps predictability. However, tuning batching+queueing on hosted frequently narrows the gap. we should run the longer test first and measure variance.
[03:38] [03:38] Ethan: security question — how are logs and KV persisted? we need SOC2 level audit logs and KMS integration.
[03:44] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II, and options for customer-managed KMS in Private. We'll share the security pack in the next email.
[03:51] Diego: also note: for the KV cache, keys are ephemeral and encrypted at rest; we can enable customer KMS for on-prem/private.
[03:58] Priya: any gotchas with quantization? we talked about 4-bit earlier.
[04:02] Diego: quantization reduces memory footprint and can increase throughput but can add small regression in output quality for some prompts. we suggest running a quality eval against your key prompt set in parallel. that's part of Redwood Optimize.
[04:13] [04:13] Tom: ok, the practical plan: run two 12-hour tests — one with concurrency 64 + batching 20ms, another with concurrency 64 + batching 50ms + KV cache enabled. both replaying sticky user keys. compare p50/p90/p99 and cost.
[04:26] Maya: yes and we'll add an extra pass where we reroute low-priority endpoints to a quantized variant to measure cost savings and failure modes.
[04:34] Sana: what do you need from us to start?
[04:36] Diego: the trace CSV with user keys + peak windows, confirmation of endpoints that are eligible for reroute, and any throughput caps your infra needs.
[04:43] Sana: I'll get the trace and endpoint list today. Tom will validate the traicer can do sticky sessions.
[04:48] [04:48] Riley: I'll kick off the staging runs once Diego pushes the config; expect initial 1-hour sanity test then full 12-hour overnight.
[04:54] Maya: timeline — we'll aim to have preliminary numbers by Friday 2027-09-24, and a follow-up sync next Wednesday 2027-09-29.
[05:01] Aisha: sounds good. small ask — can Redwood produce cost-per-1M-token and p99 tradeoff curves for the runs? that helps exec-level decisions.
[05:09] Maya: yes we'll add that to the benchmark sheet.
[05:13] [05:13] Diego: last note: we saw a small extreme tail event in one run where a single request spiked to 6s — investigating but likely due to a bad kernel scheduling from the older driver image; we've pinned the image now.
[05:24] Tom: good catch.
[05:26] Maya: ok wrapping — action items recap in chat, Diego will update config and run tests, Sana/Tom provide traces, Maya will update pricing/bench sheet. Any final questions?
[05:36] Sana: none. thanks everyone.
[05:38] Maya: thanks all, bye.

End of call.
